lines.text: We followed the humming down. There was nowhere else to go.
The last stair ended in a vault so big the lamplight couldn't find the walls. And in the middle of it stood a stone.
Not a Measuring Stone. Something far bigger. A great pillar of pale rimeglass, taller than the keep at Greyhollow, veined with blue light that moved inside it like slow water.
The Heartstone. The College whispers about it. Nobody I ever knew had seen it.
Don't say fascinating.
I wasn't going to. ...It is, though.
Around its foot, iron bars made a cage, like a birdcage around the root of a tree. And inside the cage, chained to the stone, sat a woman.
She was so thin she was almost part of it. Her long dark hair hung over her face. Frost lay on her skin like dust. And she was humming.
Slow and low, like wind going round a chimney. The song I had hummed to six frightened children. The song I never learned.
An iron plate hung on the bars, stamped with old words. Tamsin held her lamp up to it, and read it aloud.
Subject E. Greyhollow. Taken fifteen winters ago.
Greyhollow. Fifteen winters ago, I was two years old, in my father's house, far to the south. I never saw Greyhollow until last year.
But Bram had been its steward for fifty years. Whoever she was, Bram had known her.
Ash went to the bars before anyone could stop him. He lay down in front of them with his head on his paws, and whined, very softly, like a puppy.
The humming stopped.
She lifted her head, and her hair fell away from her face. A thin face, and very tired. Her eyes were grey.
Somewhere, a painting in a locked room tried to come back to me. I didn't let it. Not down there.
She looked at Ash. Then past him, at me. And she smiled, as if she had been waiting a very long time, and had always known I would come.
Lucan?
She knew my name. Nobody had said it. Nobody had told her.
Lucan. You got so tall.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and five, coming soon.
